about: The weather data supply chain as a graph: where a forecast, a warning or a picture on a weather site comes from, down to the instruments. This file is the index and the grammar: the layers (node types, each in its own small file under nodes/), the verbs (each with its inverse, each in its own small file under edges/) and the rules. Built into one file at meteorology/graph.json by the site's build.
grammar: https://graphs.sgit.ai/llms.txt : a node is just a node; every edge is a verb with a distinct inverse; no generic "related to" edge; meaning is in the edges.
rules: Every edge carries `source` (the provider's own documentation or attribution page where one exists), `read_utc` (when our reader fetched it), `state` and a short `quote`.

state "stated": every phrase in `expect` was on the page at read_utc. "not found in this read": the page answered but the phrases were not on it: the edge is unconfirmed and drawn dashed. "not read": the address did not answer 200, or we do not request it (terms).
An edge with "to": null and state "not stated" means the site does not say where its picture comes from on the address read (`searched` lists the names looked for). It is never guessed.
`label` is "fact" by default (read on the page of the body the edge is about); "evidence" where the statement is someone else's reading (named in `note`).

Ids are stable: obs-, model-, data-, body-, svc-, site- (site ids are incident.weatherwatch@'s, prefixed). incident.entities@ may adopt any node; each has an entity-shaped file at meteorology/nodes/<id>.json on the site.
Not a warning service: the graph explains and attributes; it forecasts nothing.

layers.question: Who turns it into a warning

verbs.means: An aggregator republishes the warnings of the services that issue them.
A model takes an observing system's measurements as its starting state (data assimilation), or a machine-learned model is trained on or started from another product.
A body issues warnings through its warning service, or names storms.
A body operates an observing system.
A body publishes a data set or API; or a data set carries a model's output.
A service passes on another body's model output or observations, in its own format.
A body runs a forecast model.
A forecast provider supplies a site with its forecasts (the site says so).
A site or app draws a model's output or an observing system's data. "to": null means the site does not say where its picture comes from on the address read: never guessed.
A warning service says what its warnings or forecasts are based on. Most services do not say which model stands behind a given warning: a forecaster decides.
